extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, taxonomists, and museum/field biologists working on freshwater invertebrates (sponges, polyzoa, hydra)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines for preparing, examining, and describing freshwater invertebrate specimens (Spongillidæ, Hydra, freshwater polyzoa, statoblasts, gemmules) and the structure/contents expected in taxonomic species accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of Spongillidæ
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve Spongillidæ.--Spongillidæ must be preserved dry or in very strong alcohol. Formalin should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve either dry or in very strong alcohol; do NOT use formalin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning siliceous sponge spicules
rubrics_metrics.description: To clean siliceous sponge spicules.--Place small fragments of the dried sponge (if alcohol is present, the reaction is apt to be violent) in a test tube, cover them with strong nitric acid and boil over the flame ... Add a large quantity of water to the acid and filter through pure cellulose filter-paper, agitating the liquid repeatedly. Pass clean water in considerable quantities through the filter-paper and dry the latter carefully; place it in a spirally coiled wire and ignite with a match, holding the wire in such a way that the spicules released by the burning of the paper fall into a suitable receptacle. They may then be picked up with a camel's-hair brush and mounted in Canada balsam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise protocol: (1) dry small fragments; (2) cover with strong nitric acid and boil until solids disappear; (3) dilute with large quantity water; (4) filter on pure cellulose paper and wash thoroughly; (5) dry filter, coil and ignite so spicules fall into receptacle; (6) pick spicules with a camel-hair brush and mount in Canada balsam. Caution: if alcohol present, reaction may be violent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine skeleton of a Spongillid
rubrics_metrics.description: To examine the skeleton of a Spongillid.--Cut thin hand-sections with a sharp scalpel, dehydrate if necessary, and mount in Canada balsam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare thin hand-sections with sharp scalpel; dehydrate (if needed); mount in Canada balsam for microscopic examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of gemmules for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare gemmules for examination.--Place the gemmules dry in a watch-glass with a few drops of strong nitric acid. When gas is given off freely add water in considerable quantities. Remove the gemmules with a camel's-hair brush to clean water, then to 50%, 70%, 90% and absolute alcohol in succession, leaving them for an hour in each strength of spirit. Clear with oil of cloves and mount in Canada balsam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol: (1) treat dry gemmules with strong nitric acid until effervescence subsides, dilute heavily with water; (2) transfer via camel-hair brush into successive alcohol series (50%, 70%, 90%, absolute), ~1 hour each; (3) clear with oil of cloves; (4) mount in Canada balsam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain presence of bubble-cells in Spongillid parenchyma
rubrics_metrics.description: To ascertain the presence of bubble-cells in the parenchyma of a Spongillid.--Tease up a small piece of the sponge with a pair of needles, mount under a thin cover-slip in strong spirit, and examine under a high power of the microscope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanically tease tissue with needles, mount in strong spirit under thin cover-slip, examine at high magnification to detect bubble-cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Hydra in an expanded condition
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve Hydra in an expanded condition.--Place the polyp in a watch-glass of clean water and wait until its tentacles are expanded. Heat a few drops of commercial formaldehyde and squirt the liquid while still hot at the Hydra, which will be killed instantaneously. Remove it to a solution of formaldehyde and spirit of the following formula:-- Commercial formaldehyde 1 part. Absolute alcohol 3 parts. Distilled water 7 parts. Then pass the Hydra through 50% and 70% alcohol and keep in 90%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol: (1) wait for full expansion in clean water; (2) squirt hot commercial formaldehyde to instant-kill in expanded state; (3) transfer to fixative formula: 1 part commercial formaldehyde : 3 parts absolute alcohol : 7 parts distilled water; (4) dehydrate through 50% and 70% alcohol to storage in 90%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine nettle-cell (cnidocyst) capsules
rubrics_metrics.description: To examine the capsules of the nettle-cells.--Place a living Hydra in a small drop of water on a slide and press a thin cover-slip down upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use living material: mount in a small drop and press with a thin cover-slip to observe cnidocysts under the microscope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve freshwater polyzoa in an expanded condition
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve freshwater polyzoa in an expanded condition.--Place the polyzoa in a glass tube full of clean water and allow them to expand their tentacles. Drop on them gradually when they are fully expanded a 2% aqueous solution of cocaine, two or three drops at a time, until movement ceases in the tentacles. Then pour commercial formaldehyde into the tube in considerable quantities. Allow the whole to stand for half an hour. If it is proposed to stain the specimens for anatomical investigation, they should then be removed through 50% and 70% to 90% alcohol. If, on the other hand, it is desired to keep them in a life-like condition they may be kept permanently in a solution of one part of commercial formaldehyde in four parts of water. Care must be taken that the process of paralyzing the polypides is not unduly prolonged, and it is always as well to preserve duplicate specimens in spirit or formalin with the lophophore retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol options: (A) Expanded-preservation: paralyses with incremental drops of 2% aqueous cocaine until tentacles stop moving, then fix with abundant commercial formaldehyde, stand 30 minutes, then process through alcohol series if staining; (B) For life-like permanent preservation: store in 1 part commercial formaldehyde : 4 parts water. Always avoid overly prolonged paralysis and keep duplicate specimens fixed with lophophore retracted for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of statoblasts for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare statoblasts for examination.--Place the statoblasts for a few minutes in strong nitric acid. Then remove the acid with water, pass through alcohol, clear with oil of cloves, and mount in a small quantity of Canada balsam under a cover-slip, taking care that the statoblasts lie parallel to the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol: (1) brief strong nitric acid treatment; (2) wash with water; (3) pass through graded alcohols; (4) clear in oil of cloves; (5) mount in small Canada balsam under cover-slip with statoblasts oriented parallel to cover-slip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of a taxonomic species account (required sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical sections appearing in species accounts: Zoarium, Zooecia, Polypide, Statoblast(s), Type, Geographical distribution, Biology, Illustrations/Measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each species description should include discrete headings covering the colony (zoarium) form, individual zooecia morphology, polypide structures (tentacle number, stomach form, measurements), statoblast morphology/measurements, type locality/museum depository, geographical distribution, biological notes (habitat, seasonality, associations), and referenced illustrations/figures with magnifications and labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative morphological reporting (measurements & counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give measurements and counts for diagnostic structures: e.g., 'The polypide has normally about 60 tentacles'; 'statoblast measures on an average about 0.85 × 0.56 mm'; 'polypide extended part measures rather less than 3 mm'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numerical data (counts, dimensions) with units and averages where possible, and state variability (e.g., 'variable in shape and size', ranges, or variant forms). Include magnifications for figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential diagnosis against similar taxa
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish species explicitly by listing characters by which it 'only differs from' or 'is distinguished from' related species (e.g., presence/absence of bubble-cells; amount of spongin; length and arrangement of gemmule-spicules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comparative statements enumerating which characters separate the taxon from close relatives, ideally numbered or itemized for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type designation and depository statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate type material and its repository (e.g., 'TYPE in the Indian Museum', 'TYPES in the Indian Museum', 'The statoblasts mounted ... must be regarded as the types').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the type status (holotype, type series, figures cited) and the museum or collection where types are deposited, to enable future reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations and figure legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plates/figures with labeled parts and stated magnifications (e.g., 'Fig. 46.--Lophopodella carteri ... A=outline ... × 4; C=statoblast, × 75').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear figure labels, identify anatomical parts in legends, and include magnification factors for each image component to support morphological claims.
